Official ratings for the fieldMoment of Light's Newton Abbot win time/quality vs Steel Fixer's June Rasen figureWhether Steel Fixer has resolved the Hexham jumping issue since PU
Moment of Light is the logical pick and I agree with the model. She arrives off a convincing hurdles debut win at Newton Abbot (16f167y, Good) only 19 days ago — clean completion, no jumping scar, and the trip maps closely to today’s 16f110y test. Dan Skelton / Harry Skelton are elite NH connections in strong recent form (T14 5-26, J14 5-24; #4/#3 on this card), and she is 1-1 on Good. In a field where most rivals are unraced or barely raced over hurdles, a proven finisher at this trip with hot yard/jockey numbers is the right default.

The main risk is sample size: one hurdle start and no Market Rasen course form, stepping into Class 3 against Steel Fixer, who was fourth here over this exact C+D in June (beaten only 0.2L) and is flagged as likely to lead in a mixed/contested pace map — though his Hexham PU and the flat run since weaken the jumping/fitness case versus Moment of Light’s fresher profile. Vietnorm’s 1-1 C/D record is offset by a 120-day break and a Cartmel PU (0/7); Lynxman, Blue To Blue, Pass The Buck and debutant Two Steppin lack comparable hurdle credentials at this trip.

Official ratings for unrated rivalsMarket Rasen course formWhether Elated's front-running style gets pressured at this trip
Elated is the most substantiated hurdler here: OR 98 (only rated runner), five starts with clean jumping, and a narrow second (0.3L) at Worcester 22 days ago — the clearest recent hurdle evidence in the field. Fontwell third over 19f on good offers some stamina support for this 16f110y step-up, and he looks the likely pace driver, which suits a maiden where rivals are mainly debutants or lightly raced. I would not treat the short price as proof — Ben Pauling and Ben Jones are 0-7 and 0-5 in the last fortnight — but on form and completion he still leads.

The biggest risk is trip and profile mismatch: his best work is at around 2m (Worcester twice), and the Worcester flop (15th) before the rebound shows inconsistency; a true 2m6f test on good may find him out despite the rating edge. Mighty Dink is the main danger if Dan/Harry Skelton’s second-run improvement pattern applies after a poor Sedgefield debut, while No More Teardrops brings a 16f good NH-flat win but off a 178-day break and untested over hurdles.

He is top on the numbers (OR 133), handles Good (3-9), and is the most reliable chaser here on local evidence (2-4 course, 2-3 CD), including the October 2025 win over this trip; recent Bangor third confirms he is still competitive at around three miles. Fringill Dike is the clear danger on July form here (2nd over this C&D, prior course win), but he is 6lb worse off on ratings, has had an 83-day gap, and his trainer is cold (T14 0-1). Jet To Vegas is hard to trust after a Punchestown pull-up with only four chase starts, and Nickelforce is 14lb below the top on OR with 0-4 course form despite a hot Ben Case/Harry Bannister patch.

The biggest risk to Sure Touch is not ability but execution: mixed recent chasing figures (3rd/4th/3rd), a cold Olly Murphy yard (T14 0-10), and a 5lb claimer in a race where Fringill Dike knows the track and may lead from the front. Matoury post-layoff homework and fresh stable formTraveling Soldier hurdle-only completion/jumping record vs chase-heavy profileAnnie Don OR and true readiness after 284-day absence
Traveling Soldier is the logical default: OR 86 with 11-2 looks well treated against Matoury (91) and the rest, Olly Murphy/Sean Bowen are among the stronger NH connections on the card, and he is comparatively race-fit (LR16) with a recent hurdle third at Worcester (2L, no jumping failure). The model’s “handles today’s ground” is only partly borne out (0-2 on Good), but his chase profile over ~20f suggests stamina for 23f, and he is tagged as likely forward in a mixed pace map, which suits a handicapper who can dictate or sit handy rather than a hold-up horse needing everything to fall right.

The main danger is Matoury, who has won this exact course, trip, and going twice (July and June at Market Rasen 23f Good C5) and was only 1.5L third here in June 2025 form cycle—course-D form the favourite cannot match. That case is weakened by 68 days off, the Cartmel “never travelled” report, and hold-up tactics if Annie Don, The Clonmel Kid, and Traveling Soldier burn it out; Electric Eddy is a secondary threat if the Twiston-Davies yard’s hot T14 form transfers to this trip. I stay with the baseline pick rather than rubber-stamping Matoury on CD alone.

The model's top pick is justified by the trainer/jockey combination and weight, but Matoury's recent course-distance victory and Electric Eddy's experience make them the main risks.

Chester six days ago was the clearest recent signal — won a competitive 6f handicap off draw 10 with Sean Kirrane, beating a deep field at 5.0 despite the routine post-race test note. That run sits on top of useful 6f form (4-17 at the trip) and a hold-up style that should suit a **soft Haydock 6f** where the pace map flags Cape Ashizuri and himself as likely leaders in a **contested** setup; high-draw bias here (43% of winners) also fits stall 10. The Doncaster flop reads as a one-off after a big price rather than the true level — Art Lover and Rousing Encore are solid each-way profiles (Haggas/Fallon momentum; 2nd on soft at Ayr last time), but neither has stamped authority like Miraculous’s Chester win, and several market leaders carry negatives: Black Star Boy/So Darn Hot are split from the Walker yard with patchy 6f soft evidence, Cape Ashizuri is a NR here with a forward trip, and Zain Primus is AW-bred with no soft-turf proof from draw 14.
